title: pendingReward() view still over-reports when balance is insufficient, now desynchronized from the revert-on-shortfall claim path
regression-risk: pre-existing with amplified UX impact (CS-07 from prior audit, now interacts with story-002 revert)
description:
`pendingReward(address)` returns `(user.amount * acc) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt` — the full theoretical entitlement — without clamping against `rewardToken.balanceOf(this)`. Under the prior code this caused silent-forfeiture display drift (covered in CS-01/CS-07). Under the new `_safePay` revert semantics, the consequence is different but still problematic: a UI or keeper reading `pendingReward()` and then calling `claim()` will see the transaction REVERT on the `_safePay` shortfall check, with no indication of how much the user could actually claim at that moment.

The view also does not project `dispatcherHook.pull()` — so even a user who COULD claim after a fresh pull will see `pendingReward` underreport the claimable amount (because the pending mint-debt is not yet folded into `accRewardPerShare`). The combination is confusing: the view can simultaneously over-report (ignoring balance cap) and under-report (ignoring pending hook debt).
impact: Frontends and keepers will display inaccurate figures and will issue claim transactions that revert in shortfall conditions, consuming gas and producing a poor UX. In automated claim bots, this can lead to wasted gas and failed claim loops. Not a direct loss-of-funds issue.
proof: Read line 339: `return (user.amount * acc) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt;`. No clamp against balance. Also the `acc` computed in lines 331-338 does not fold in `dispatcherHook.mintDebt()`. Call `pendingReward(user)` in a state where balance < entitlement and then attempt `claim()` — the tx reverts in `_safePay` while the view promised the full entitlement.
suggested-fix: Two changes: (a) add a balance clamp — `return min(entitlement, rewardToken.balanceOf(this))` — so the view matches what `claim()` would actually pay or reject. (b) Optionally, project the pending dispatcher mint-debt into `acc` before computing entitlement, giving users a forward-looking view of what a sync-plus-claim would yield. Document the semantics clearly in NatSpec.
